prose_grades.quote: sha256 is 64 hex characters, and only in the 12-63 range can a short pin be *compared at all*: a pin there is an *abbreviation*, still honoured ... but reported loudly as reduced strength.  A pin of 1-11 hex is REFUSED as a mismatch: ``_same_digest`` requires ``width >= 12``, so it cannot be compared AT ALL (fail-closed) — never a weaker match, and with no ``PIN ABBREVIATED`` note.  A pin of 65+ hex is refused as over-long.

The rule (U8.19, corrected by U8.24): in the *comparable* range a pin is reported at **every** such length, 63 hex exactly as loudly as 12 ... That range is 12-63 hex, not "every length below 64": below 12 hex the pin is not warned about but REFUSED, because ``_same_digest`` requires ``width >= 12``, so a 1-11-hex pin cannot be compared at all and lands in the mismatch branch (fail-closed, no ``PIN ABBREVIATED`` note).

The trailing ``width >= 12`` is a floor, not a tolerance: a pin of 12-63 hex that matches is still honoured — 12 hex is the historical minimum ... A pin of 1-11 hex returns False here: it cannot be compared at all, so it is refused as a mismatch (fail-closed) rather than accepted at reduced strength.

an abbreviated pin of 12-63 hex characters is accepted only with a ``PIN ABBREVIATED`` note and a ``REDUCED STRENGTH`` clause, while a pin shorter than 12 hex cannot be compared at all (``_same_digest`` needs ``width >= 12``) and is therefore refused as a mismatch, fail-closed, without that note; and an over-long pin (more than 64 hex characters) is refused
